text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Snow and ice over Europe, death toll rises
- Kohl calls for deep changes in the way Germans live
- Transport ministry opposed to motorway toll
- Major waterways except for Rhine closed because of ice
- Oil to be cheaper from mid 1997
- Christmas gift vouchers to boost retail trade into January
- Tietmeyer says fundamental conditions must be created for economic upturn
HANDELSBLATT
- Kohl says stability pact boosts chances for single currency
- Export to continue to drive economy in 1997
- German firms step up investment abroad, particularly in Asia and South America
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Social Democrat (SPD) leaders Lafontaine and Schroeder at odds about European single currency
- Two state premiers call for 80 mark annual motorway toll
- Chancellor Kohl calls on Germans to change their ways
- Construction industry expects to cut jobs despite new minimum wage
DIE WELT
- Chancellor Kohl calls on Germans to change their ways
- New row breaks out over proposal to levy motorway toll
- Employers and unions to try to revive consensus in pay negotiations
-- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 26097160
